brand.name: Travel Safe
brand.tagline: A safety net that checks on you.

hero.eyebrow: Safety check-ins for people who travel alone
hero.description: Check in with one tap on a schedule you choose. Miss it, and the people you trust get a private page with your last known location, SOS media and the last 7 days of your route.
hero.note: No tracking. No ads. You decide who is told.

features.title: Built for the moment nobody picks up.
features.description: Most safety apps stop at a panic button. Travel Safe keeps working when your phone is off, your battery is gone, or you simply cannot reach it.

items.title: One-tap check-ins
items.body: Set a rhythm that fits your day, from 15 minutes to 30 days. Every check-in resets the clock and clears any active emergency.

items.title: A dead-man switch that runs server-side
items.body: The hourly worker watches your deadline even when your phone is off. You get a warning first. After the grace period, your contacts get the private page.

items.title: SOS video, audio, images or a message
items.body: Send up to 25 MB of media or a short custom message. Everything is stored in R2 and shown on the same private page as your location.

items.title: Private, revocable pages
items.body: Every contact gets a unique link. Revoke one contact without touching the others, or rotate your own link and kill every old copy instantly.

how.title: Three steps. No dashboard to babysit.

steps.title: Check in
steps.body: One API call, or one tap in the app you build on top of it. Your location is saved for 7 days and your deadline moves forward.

steps.title: Miss the deadline
steps.body: At the deadline the worker warns you by email. After the grace period it triggers the dead-man switch and notifies your emergency contacts.

steps.title: They open the page
steps.body: A private, no-login page shows your latest location, a 7-day trail and any SOS media. The owner can revoke access at any time.

developer.title: An API you can build a safety product on.
developer.body: The Go API runs on Cloudflare Workers, stores structured data in D1 and media in R2. A separate TypeScript worker owns the hourly switch. No servers to patch, no queues to run.
bullets: D1 relational storage with 7-day location retention
R2 for SOS video, audio and images
Hourly dead-man switch with styled email alerts

items.q: Is Travel Safe an emergency service?
items.a: No. It notifies the people you choose. It does not contact police, ambulance or fire services and cannot guarantee that anyone will see an alert. If someone is in immediate danger, call local emergency services.

items.q: What happens if my phone is off?
items.a: The switch lives on Cloudflare's edge, not on your phone. The hourly worker checks your last check-in against your deadline and can trigger the alert even if your device is offline.

items.q: How long is location data kept?
items.a: Location points are retained for 7 days and then deleted by the hourly worker. The private page only queries that 7-day window.

items.q: Can a contact keep the link forever?
items.a: Only until you revoke it. Each contact has their own token. Revoking one contact leaves the others working, and rotating your owner link invalidates all previous copies.

items.q: How do I run it myself?
items.a: The repository includes the Go API, the TypeScript worker, D1 migrations and the React site. You need a Cloudflare account, a D1 database, an R2 bucket and an email provider.

cta.title: Build your own safety net.
cta.body: Start with one user, one interval and one trusted contact. Add SOS media and private pages when you need them.

footer.tagline: A safety net, not an emergency service.

support.title: How can we help?
support.description: Travel Safe is an open project. Report a bug, ask for a feature, or read the docs before you deploy your own instance.
support.issuesBody: Bugs, feature requests and documentation fixes live in the public repository. Include your API version, what you expected, and what happened.
support.securityBody: Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. Use GitHub's private security advisory flow so we can fix it before it is disclosed.
support.statusBody: The API exposes a health endpoint with its version and current UTC time. The scheduler also exposes a health endpoint.
support.docsBody: The documentation covers authentication, check-ins, contacts, SOS uploads, emergency pages, the hourly worker and self-hosting.

faq.q: An emergency link says it is invalid.
faq.a: The account owner rotated their link or revoked that contact. Ask them for the current link.

faq.q: The worker is not sending email.
faq.a: Set RESEND_API_KEY or configure a Cloudflare send_email binding, then verify EMAIL_FROM is on an onboarded sending domain. Without a provider the worker logs the alert and retries.

faq.q: How do I delete an account?
faq.a: Call DELETE /v1/me with the account's API key. This removes the user, contacts, locations, check-ins, SOS records and emergency events.

emergency.supportBody: Try to reach them directly. If you believe someone is in immediate danger, contact local emergency services. This page is not monitored around the clock.
emergency.invalidBody: The link may have been revoked by the account owner, or it may never have existed. Ask the owner for a current link.
emergency.footer: Travel Safe shares only what the account owner chose to share. The owner can revoke this link at any time.

notFound.title: This page wandered off.
notFound.body: The link is broken or the page has moved. The emergency viewer links are private and look like /emergency/<token>.
